topic.title: Auxiliary supervision utility in the strongest joint model
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, does auxiliary-task supervision improve click AUC in the strongest joint model, and does its influence on shared representations explain any benefit or harm?
topic.hypothesis: Auxiliary supervision may provide useful shared-representation learning or introduce gradient interference. This is unverified at the stronger joint starting point. Compare its unchanged supervision with click-only supervision and controlled auxiliary-gradient participation, preserving historical actions, task masks, representation capacity and training exposure. Use replacement controls to distinguish informative auxiliary supervision from generic optimization effects; measure training and inference cost and repeat decisive contrasts. No reproducible advantage over click-only supervision would falsify useful auxiliary supervision in this setting. An advantage without discriminating gradient controls would leave the interference explanation unresolved.
